summary: Review-remediated HR employment domain foundation in the flat hr microservice layout, with hardened metadata-only refs, stable Korea labor-obligation identity/effective-date/idempotency, and complete multispectrum facets.

findings: Remediated suite-shaped crate placement by moving the implementation to the flat hr microservice path and narrowing the crate to the employment bounded context.
Domain model remains small: EmployeeCreate, Employee::new, Employee::lifecycle_event, LegalEntityWorkforceSnapshot, and evaluate_labor_compliance.
Flat microservice layout avoids suite coupling and supports independent HR scaling/release/SLO ownership.
The slice claims only pure domain invariants; measured SLOs, runtime APIs, filings, and ERP parity remain explicitly outside scope.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Domain rejects missing legal entity, prefix-only tenant/rulepack ids, traversal-shaped legal entity/workflow/evidence refs, token-shaped evidence refs, public employee data class, invalid rulepack effective date, and non-hrev lifecycle event ids.
findings: Negative fixtures pass under cargo test -p oya-hr-employment-domain.
The crate is discoverable under microservices/hr/README.md and its package metadata follows oya-hr-employment-domain naming.
Validation failures use typed HrDomainError variants instead of silent defaults.
Verification after review remediation passed: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo test -p oya-hr-employment-domain; cargo clippy -p oya-hr-employment-domain --all-targets -- -D warnings.
cargo deny, cargo-prefix, slo-coverage, dependency-seam, catalog validate, and broad data-class are recorded separately in the verification block with pass/pre-existing-blocker status.

alternatives_named: Implement the full HR/payroll/accounting runtime in one changeset
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: ADR-0131/ADR-0132 flat microservice doctrine is newer and higher-fit for architecture than suite-shaped crate naming; the employment bounded context gives a small reviewable HR foundation.
rejected_reasons: Root crates/ oya-enterprise-hr-domain risks reintroducing enterprise suite as an architecture boundary.
A full runtime stack in one changeset would create false production readiness claims and conflict-prone write scopes.

findings: Employee PII is classified as PII_IDENTIFYING; tenant_id and legal_entity_id are mandatory and classified internal.
Evidence refs are metadata-only and reject token/secret/bearer/password-shaped material, prefix-only values, whitespace/control characters, traversal segments, and backslashes.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: No previous HR implementation existed; no hot-path runtime or allocation budget is claimed.

findings.summary: The change adds pure constructors and threshold evaluation only; no storage/network/async hot path or query loop is introduced.

findings: Korea labor obligations are represented as rulepack/effective-date scoped evidence obligations, not as live filing/certification claims.
All new public struct fields in the crate carry data_class comments; broad repo data-class gate still has an unrelated pre-existing blocker.

The slice is additive: one new microservice folder, one new workspace package, catalog rows, and spec/test-ref alignment. Rollback removes those paths and the workspace member; no migration or persisted data exists.
No runtime telemetry is introduced because the slice is domain-only. Future app/rest/worker slices must emit lifecycle/obligation events to audit-chain and OpenTelemetry before production claims.
specs/microservices/hr.json was aligned from earlier oya-enterprise-hr-* planned names to oya-hr-employment-* paths under ADR-0131/ADR-0132. No external API compatibility exists yet.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: Implementing HR ahead of cloud integration is useful only if the slice follows flat microservice doctrine and avoids false ERP/payroll-production claims.
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: HR/payroll/accounting would remain planned-only, blocking later enterprise cloud integration.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: Waiting for full suite/runtime integration would preserve a zero-code gap; a pure domain slice creates testable invariants without runtime claims.

findings: Fits the system as a flat HR microservice with Payroll and Accounting as separate services composed through refs/events, not a suite wrapper.
Review-agent architecture blocker was resolved by relocation/renaming and spec alignment.
Package name oya-hr-employment-domain follows oya-<ms>-<bc>-<layer>.
microservices/hr/README.md and PRD.md provide required layout entrypoints while pointing at the machine-readable HR spec.
Implementation resides under microservices/hr/crates/oya-hr-employment-domain with per-service catalog and central registry aggregation row.
No storage, network, workflow execution, regulator filing, or payroll/accounting runtime coupling is introduced.
The package depends only on oya-data-boundary-kernel.
HR AC-01..AC-03 acceptance refs point to existing flat HR crate tests.
HR AC-04 leave/payroll-impact and AC-05 sensitive-read policy refs are explicitly marked PENDING in specs/microservices/hr.json and are not claimed by CS-ENT-HR-001.
Threshold evaluation is deterministic and rulepack/effective-date scoped; no approximate or heuristic payroll/compliance calculation is claimed.
